title: The Flannan Isles Keepers
subtitle: Eilean Mòr · Outer Hebrides, 1900
voice_instructions: Measured, quiet, a little hushed — calm and unhurried, but with a touch more forward energy than a long documentary; the cold voice of something that read the whole file. Never sensational. Small pauses.
grade: Desaturated documentary still, a remote rocky island in the Outer Hebrides of Scotland in winter 1900, a stone lighthouse, sheer cliffs, heavy grey Atlantic sea, cold blue-grey overcast light, melancholy and uncanny, cinematic wide composition, fine film grain. Single image, not a collage, no text, no signage, no people, no faces.

beats.vo: Eilean Mòr, in the Outer Hebrides. December, nineteen hundred. A passing ship saw that the island's lighthouse was dark.
beats.img: A tall stone lighthouse standing dark and unlit on the summit of a steep grassy island rising from a heavy grey Atlantic sea at dusk, sheer rock cliffs, no lamp burning, remote and silent.

beats.vo: Weather held off the relief boat until Boxing Day. When it landed, the three keepers were gone.
beats.img: A small wooden rowing boat approaching a concrete landing stage at the foot of tall wet rock cliffs, a long stone stairway climbing up the cliff face, grey swell, overcast winter light, no people.

beats.vo: The lamps were cleaned and ready. The clock had stopped. One set of oilskins was still inside.
beats.img: The interior of a plain 1900 lighthouse keepers' kitchen, a tidy scrubbed wooden table, a cast-iron stove, a wall clock, a single dark oilskin coat hanging on a hook by the door, cold grey window light, no people.

beats.vo: At the west landing, iron railings were twisted, and a block of stone weighing over a ton had been moved.
beats.img: Twisted and bent iron railings around a small crane platform on a wet rock landing above a churning grey sea, a large displaced stone block nearby, spray and torn turf, stormy winter light, no people.

beats.vo: The inquiry believed a great wave had swept them away. No trace of the three men was ever found.
beats.img: A vast empty grey Atlantic sea under low winter cloud seen from a high island cliff top, a distant unlit lighthouse silhouette on the headland, long swells rolling in, cold and unresolved, no people.

facts.claim: Flannan Isles lighthouse is on Eilean Mòr, Flannan Isles, Outer Hebrides; three keepers vanished December 1900
A passing steamer (Archtor) noted around midnight on 15 December 1900 that the light was not lit
Relief vessel Hesperus was delayed by weather and reached the island on 26 December 1900 (Boxing Day); keepers James Ducat, Thomas Marshall, Donald McArthur were missing
Lamps trimmed/cleaned and ready for lighting
One set of oilskins was left inside (two sets of outdoor clothing missing)
West landing: iron railing round the crane platform displaced and twisted; block of stone upwards of 20 cwt (about a ton) dislodged (Muirhead report, NRS NLC3/1/1)
Superintendent Muirhead's inquiry concluded the men were swept away by an unexpectedly large roller/wave
No bodies / no trace of the men was ever found
Still unexplained as of 2025-26: no new findings; retellings continue (Dec 2025, Jun 2026)
